title: Sharp Logarithmic Bounds for Vilenkin-Fej\'er Kernels
abstract:
arXiv:2611.09929v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Let $G_m$ be a bounded Vilenkin group and put $R:=\sup_j m_j$. We prove the sharp uniform estimate
  $$\|K_n\|_1\leq \frac{17}{15\ln 2}\ln R,\qquad n\geq1,$$
  for the Fej\'er kernels associated with the Vilenkin system. The constant $17/(15\ln2)$ is best possible. In the Walsh--Paley case $R=2$, the result reduces exactly to Toledo's sharp estimate $\sup_n\|K_n\|_1=17/15$.

title: Graded-Edge Rakotch Contractions in Generalized Metric Spaces with Weighted Graphs
abstract:
arXiv:2611.09996v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We introduce the notion of graded-edge Rakotch contraction mappings on a generalized metric space with a weighted graph. We prove that the successive iterate of every starting point converge uniformly to a common limit, which is the unique fixed point. We derive an explicit iteration-complexity bound and, under a relaxed triangle inequality, a geometric rate whose constant is the graph invariant. Finally, we illustrate the theory on an explicit real graded contraction that realizes the interior optimum, on a quadratic integral equation, and on finite weighted digraphs.

title: Excluding 54 of the 76 Nontrivial Factorization Patterns of the Cuboid Polynomial $P_{a,b,u}(t)$
abstract:
arXiv:2611.10012v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Let $P_{a,b,u}(t)$ be Sharipov's even monic degree-$12$ third cuboid polynomial, with positive pairwise distinct rational parameters. We prove a uniform normal form for its complete factorization over $\mathbb{Q}$. Every factorization consists of at most two even quadratic factors, even irreducible factors of higher degree, and pairs of irreducible factors exchanged by $t\mapsto-t$. After dividing all degrees by the contribution of this symmetry, the normal form satisfies one degree equation, one sign equation, and an obligatory-factor alternative: an even irreducible factor of degree at least six, or an even irreducible quartic with positive rational-square constant term. The arithmetic input is a uniform construction over $\mathbb{Q}_2$, using Newton polygons, Hensel lifting, and a norm obstruction from $\mathbb{Q}_2(i)$. Valuations at all finite primes constrain rational factor constants to signed squares, while the real root equation gives exactly two simple negative roots of the auxiliary sextic. The normal form leaves exactly $22$ of the $76$ nontrivial partitions of $12$, thereby excluding $54$ complete irreducible degree patterns by one argument. Of these exclusions, $37$ follow from evenness alone and $17$ from the additional arithmetic restrictions. All local cases are proved explicitly, and an exact verification script accompanies the algebraic identities and exhaustive partition enumeration. The remaining patterns are necessary possibilities; their realization is not asserted, and full irreducibility remains open.

title: Nonconstant Congruence Speeds of Integer Tetration in Non-Squarefree Radices
abstract:
arXiv:2611.10018v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We further develop the theory of congruence speed for integer tetration in non-squarefree numeral systems, building on Appendix B of [M. Rip\`a and G. Di Pietro (2026), A compact notation for peculiar properties characterizing integer tetration, Notes on Number Theory and Discrete Mathematics, 32(3), 477-496]. For bases coprime to the radix, we establish an eventual floor-difference representation and determine the exact spectrum of attainable least periods. We construct explicit arithmetic progressions containing infinitely many prime bases with nonconstant congruence speed for every non-squarefree radix, thereby proving the coprime-infinitude conjecture posed in Appendix B. We also derive a uniform quadratic bound for the least coprime base with nonconstant congruence speed and establish exact natural densities of nonstabilizing bases, both among integers coprime to the radix and among those not divisible by its radical, together with the corresponding relative density among primes. Finally, we give necessary and sufficient conditions for the perfect-power congruence-speed identity (Equation (2.12) of the cited paper) to hold in arbitrary radices, determine the exact least eventual period when stabilization fails, and establish a separate criterion for the boundary case of the original parameter restriction.

title: Constructive algebraic methods for bisymmetric means
authors: P\'al Burai, Gergely Kiss, Patricia Szokol
abstract:
arXiv:2611.10021v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We prove continuity for reflexive, bisymmetric binary operations that are strictly increasing in each variable, under certain algebraic conditions. In fact, for some algebraic weights we construct a weighted quasi-arithmetic representation of such functions without assuming continuity. An elementary construction gives the case $r=2/3$. More generally, a word equality whose polynomial difference has a unique simple zero $r\in(0,1)$ forces the representation with weight $r$; every algebraic $r$ with no other conjugate in $(0,1)$ arises this way. The proof uses an affine embedding and a dense-domain extension argument.

title: Cross-Domain Channel Estimation for MU-MIMO-OFDM
authors: Mingcheng Nie, Shuangyang Li, Ruoxi Chong, Giuseppe Caire, Yonghui Li
abstract:
arXiv:2611.10052v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Conventional channel estimation for multiple-input multiple-output orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (MIMO-OFDM) relies on the pilot interpolation without explicitly identifying the sparse delay-angle (DA) components. To exploit DA sparsity while maintaining backward compatibility with existing MIMO-OFDM systems, we propose a cross-domain channel estimation scheme for multiuser MIMO-OFDM (MU-MIMO-OFDM) systems. The scheme exploits the circular convolution structure in the DA domain to identify candidate DA pairs by correlating delay-domain observations with DA pilot responses. These pairs and the known pilots then define a time-frequency (TF) dictionary for refining the DA coefficients from TF observations through least-squares or sparsity-regularized fitting. The refined coefficients and candidate pairs reconstruct the aggregate channel across antennas and subcarriers aligning with the geometric channel model. Numerical results show approximately 10 dB and 7 dB lower normalized mean-square error than the conventional OFDM estimation schemes for integer and fractional delay and angle indices, respectively.

title: On the dynamics of weighted shifts on Fr\'echet sequence spaces over trees
authors: Mateus Azevedo, Fernando Costa Jr., Jo\~ao V. A. Pinto
abstract:
arXiv:2611.10053v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this paper, we give characterizations of Li--Yorke chaos, mean Li--Yorke chaos and distributional chaos for weighted backward shifts acting on general Fr\'echet sequence spaces over directed trees. As corollaries, we obtain explicit characterizations in the setting of K\"othe spaces $\lambda_p(A,V)$, where $p\in\{0\}\cup[1,\infty)$ and $V$ is a directed tree. In particular, we obtain criteria for the case of the classical Banach spaces $\ell^p(V)$, $p\in[1,\infty)$, and $c_0(V)$.

title: Prime supports and vanishing in restricted coprime representations
abstract:
arXiv:2611.10059v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study the prime supports that eliminate every representation of an even integer $N$ by two positive integers coprime to $6P$. Let $J(k)$ be the largest vanishing instance obtainable with at most $k$ factors of $P$ not dividing $N/2$. We prove $k(\log k)^2\ll J(k)\ll_\varepsilon k^{4+\varepsilon}$ for every $\varepsilon>0$. The upper bound follows by comparing a classical family of shifted-prime representations with a two-dimensional upper sieve for the loss at each additional factor. Retaining the same local density factor in both estimates yields a weighted survival criterion and positivity whenever the number of noncolliding factors above $N^\theta$ is sufficiently small compared with $N^\theta$, for fixed $0<\theta<1/4$. An exact reduction separates a minimum prime cover into forced prime-pair contributions and a residual problem, and gives the lower bound for $J$ along powers of two. Residue occupancies characterize the extremal concentration at a first zero. Explicit discrepancy estimates show that supports with at most eleven factors cannot eliminate every representation when $N>2780460$, nor supports with at most seven noncolliding factors when $N\ge2266292$. Positivity for the complete support of primes up to $\sqrt N$ remains open.

title: Operator-Adapted Multiscale Kernels for High-Contrast Elliptic Inverse Problems
abstract:
arXiv:2611.10071v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We consider the joint recovery of the state and diffusion coefficient in a high-contrast elliptic equation from sparse, noisy state measurements. We seek the coefficient in a parameterized family defined relative to a prescribed reference coefficient. We construct a generalized multiscale finite element basis from the reference coefficient and use it to define a finite-rank kernel for the state. A weak Galerkin residual enforces the equation without pointwise differentiation across material interfaces. For each trial coefficient, the state is obtained by solving a linear least-squares problem. Variable projection eliminates the state coordinates from the objective, and the reduced gradient is evaluated without an adjoint PDE solve.
  We split the state reconstruction error into multiscale approximation, penalty relaxation, and parameter estimation terms. Under an admissible patch decomposition, the squared multiscale approximation error is bounded by a local spectral tail estimate with a contrast-independent interpolation constant. For a fixed coefficient and discretization, the penalty relaxation error is of order $O(\varepsilon^2)$ when the residual weight is proportional to $\varepsilon^{-2}$. The parameter contribution is bounded by local Lipschitz continuity of the projected state. In 50 synthetic tests based on a reference medium of contrast $10^4$, the multiscale space with the weak residual gives mean relative state and log-coefficient errors of 2.37\% and 4.43\%, respectively, the lowest among the four configurations tested.

title: Double sums involving quotients of binomial coefficients
authors: Kunle Adegoke, Robert Frontczak, Karol Gryszka
abstract:
arXiv:2611.10072v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper is the third part of our detailed investigation of double sums where the inner sum is binomial but incomplete. We prove many identities for these double sums involving quotients of binomial coefficients and additional parameters. In addition, we evaluate some quadratic incomplete sums using Legendre polynomials.

title: Consistency considerations for rare-event importance sampling
authors: Jason Beh, Emilien Flayac, Jerome Morio, Florian Simatos
abstract:
arXiv:2611.10094v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We consider the problem of estimating a small probability $p = P(X \in A)$ by importance sampling with auxiliary density $g$, where $X$ is drawn according to some density $f$. We establish a simple necessary and sufficient condition for the consistency of the importance sampling estimator in triangular schemes where the dimension, the densities $f$ and $g$ and the set $A$ may evolve. It allows to refine the results of Chatterjee and Diaconis [Ann. Appl. Probab. 28 (2018), no. 2, 1099-1135] by establishing the exact minimal sample size required for consistency. Moreover, it allows to study the regime $p \to 0$ which, despite being the relevant mathematical regime for rare-event estimations, has received very little attention so far. We perform an in-depth study of the hyperplane case $A = \{x: x^\top u \geq \alpha\}$ with Gaussian densities, showing that in this case, the optimal importance sampling density considerably improves consistency compared to the standard Monte Carlo estimator. However, we conclude the paper with moment considerations which suggest that, whenever the Monte Carlo and optimal importance sampling estimators both converge, convergence may occur faster for the Monte Carlo estimator.

title: Statistical Geometry of Group Actions: Symmetry, Transport, Estimation
authors: Quentin Berthet, Peter Bartlett, Romuald Elie, Yu-Han Wu
abstract:
arXiv:2611.10111v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study variational inference in the presence of distributional symmetry, focusing on the interaction between two distinct group actions on a sample space: a symmetry action that leaves a reference distribution invariant, and a transport action that generates a parametric variational family by pushforward. By analyzing the algebraic structure of the total transformation group generated by both actions and the induced adjoint representation of the symmetry group on the transport Lie algebra, we establish that the Riemannian gradient of the Kullback--Leibler divergence at the true transport parameter is constrained to lie in the trivial representation of the symmetry group. Consequently, symmetry forces the gradient to vanish along all non-trivial representations. Combining this representation-theoretic constraint with parameter identifiability yields an orthogonal decomposition of the transport Lie algebra into three interpretable subspaces: an identifiability kernel (along which the objective is locally constant), a bias subspace (where the gradient may be nonzero due to model misspecification), and a symmetry-breaking subspace (where the gradient is forced to vanish by symmetry alone). Finally, we characterize the residual bias directions in terms of distributional mismatch between the base model and the standardized target, and derive an explicit Stein-type moment-matching condition that eliminates this bias, extending the location-scale results of (Margossian and Saul, 2025) to general Lie group transformation families.

title: Discrete Spoilers: Introducing Abstract Undergraduate Mathematics Using Graph Theory
abstract:
arXiv:2611.10143v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Students often have serious difficulties with many key concepts of the undergraduate mathematics curriculum. We argue that many of these difficulties can be eased by explicitly separating the key ideas from the technical details. To do so, we present finite graphs as a setting where the basic concepts appear more transparently, because on a graph most proofs only require basic techniques from linear algebra. We illustrate this approach in three areas that cover a large part of the curriculum. First, we explain basic operators from vector calculus, such as the gradient and the divergence, through the incidence matrix of a graph. Second, we show that the diffusion equation has a simple solution on a graph. We also solve the graph Dirichlet problem, in which the values at some vertices are fixed. Third, we introduce a second incidence matrix that illustrates homology, cohomology and the Helmholtz decomposition in a simple way. Finally, we outline how to apply this approach to other branches of mathematics.

title: Linear Response for Self-Consistent Transfer Operators on Graphons
abstract:
arXiv:2611.10167v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We develop the response theory of the equilibrium state of a large heterogeneous network of weakly coupled uniformly expanding circle maps. The thermodynamic limit of such a network is governed by a Self-Consistent Transfer Operator (STO) acting on measures fibred over a graphon $W$, as introduced in \cite{MPT2025}. We prove that in the weak coupling regime the unique attracting fixed point $\phi^\star(\alpha)$ of the STO depends on the coupling strength in a Lipschitz, and then differentiable, way in a scale of fibrewise Sobolev spaces, and we derive a linear response formula.
  Our main result is that at zero coupling the response factorises: its derivative along the fibre $z$ equals $\barW(z)\,\Up$, where $\barW$ is the degree function of the graphon and $\Up=-(\Id-P)^{-1}[P(H_\rho\rho)]'$ is a universal profile depending only on the local dynamics and on the coupling function. To first order the heterogeneity of the statistical response across the network is therefore dictated by the degree profile alone, and the finer topology is invisible; the susceptibility of a node is proportional to its degree, so hubs respond most. The topology enters at higher order through a tree expansion: the perturbative coefficients of the equilibrium, defined unconditionally by an explicit recursion, are combinations --- with universal coefficient functions --- of the rooted homomorphism densities of trees with $m$ edges. We prove that the first two coefficients are the genuine asymptotic ones, the second producing the mean degree of the neighbours of $z$. We also obtain a response formula for perturbations of the graphon itself, Green--Kubo expressions for observables, and the prediction that in a finite network the linear susceptibility of a node is proportional to its normalised degree.

title: A Hierarchical Variational Inequality Approach to Generalized Nash Equilibrium Seeking with Nonlinear Shared Constraints
authors: Tatiana Tatarenko, Puya Latafat, Alberto Bemporad
abstract:
arXiv:2611.10172v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study the computation of variational generalized Nash equilibria (v-GNE) in games with strongly monotone pseudo-gradients and nonlinear convex shared constraints. We show that the v-GNE problem is exactly equivalent to a hierarchical variational inequality, whose lower level is given by the gradient of a smooth convex penalty of the constraint violation over the local action sets. Building on this reformulation, we propose a hierarchical regularization scheme that operates entirely in the primal space and requires only projections onto the local action sets. In the centralized setting, we prove last-iterate squared distance convergence to the v-GNE with rate $O(1/t^{\scriptscriptstyle 2/3})$ under a local error bound condition, which holds, e.g., under Slater's condition, improved to $O(1/t)$ under a global error bound condition. We then extend the scheme to the partial-decision information setting, where the agents communicate over a network and maintain local estimates of the joint action. We derive a distributed algorithm with a constant stepsize operating in the primal space and converging to the v-GNE with rate $O(1/t)$.

title: Linear Convergence of Nesterov's Acceleration for All Momentum Parameter
abstract:
arXiv:2611.10205v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study the convergence rate of the Nesetrov's accelerated proximal gradient method for a smooth, strongly convex composite minimization objective across a range of value of the momentum extrapolation. The literature proves a convergence rate of the method for a specific momentum extrapolation parameter choice based on the knowledge of strong convexity and Lipschitz smoothness constants. For the heavy ball method it is established that every choice of the momentum parameter either fails to accelerate or fails to converge on the same function class. We prove in this paper that a range of Nesterov style constant momentum extrapolation parameters produces a linear convergence rate. We corroborate these results numerically via performance estimation which computes a method's exact worst case rate as a semidefinite program.

title: Laplace approximation of the parameter posterior with embedded error for efficient uncertainty quantification of expensive model calibrations
authors: Reese E. Jones, Kyle N. Karlson, Matt W. Kury, Moe Khalil, Ray S. Tuminaro
abstract:
arXiv:2611.10210v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In practical engineering, there is a clear need for uncertainty quantification (UQ) of models used in design because forward UQ puts probabilities on performance predictions. However, without surrogate building, most forward engineering models are too expensive for traditional UQ methods like Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling. Our goal is to provide inexpensive, approxi- mate UQ that can be applied after an expensive traditional least squares fit, where the UQ handles both uncorrelated noise and parameter variance as in the embedded-error treatment developed by Sargsyan, Najm, and Ghanem (2015). After developing the basic theory to connect a Laplace-like approximation to Bayesian calibration, we compare the proposed method to black-box variational inference in terms of cost and fidelity. Then we demonstrate the method on real-world calibration of solid material models.

title: The microstructure of information through mean field learning interaction
authors: Panagiotis E. Souganidis, Renyuan Xu, Thaleia Zariphopoulou
abstract:
arXiv:2611.10244v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study how knowledge about partially observable model parameters is being created and propagated in large scale systems. Information is generated from observational signals whose dynamics depend endogenously on the learning history, the learning duration, the decisions and the related costs encountered by a continuum of decision makers. Such characteristics give rise to a new class of sequential testing problems in which there is continuous endogenous feedback. Adopting the classical approach of Shiryaev, we relate the problem to an optimal stopping one for the representative belief process, whose generator now depends on the evolving interactions. Considering a fixed point for the latter, we introduce a notion of mean field game and prove the existence of an equilibrium. Our arguments, which are based on a combination of pde and probabilistic techniques, involve a detailed analysis of the underlying variational inequality and the geometry, stability and continuity of the free boundaries.

title: Transport Less, Solve Faster: Exploiting sparsity in algorithm design for Unbalanced Optimal Transport
authors: Gennaro Auricchio, Francesco Rinaldi, Saverio Salzo, Giovanni Spisso
abstract:
arXiv:2611.10268v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this paper, we study the computational aspects of the Unbalanced Optimal Transport (UOT) problem between two given positive measures $\mu$ and $
u$. The UOT is a variant to the classic Optimal Transportation problem in which the linear constraints modeling mass preservation are relaxed and replaced by a convex penalty $\Dphi$ in the objective function. First, we show that any UOT problem admits a discrete solution as long as $\mu$ and $
u$ are discrete, allowing us to express the optimality conditions characterizing the solution to the UOT problem in an easy-to-handle form. By exploiting the optimality conditions we provide an upper and lower bound on the marginals of the solution as well as a bound on the mass that any solution assigns to any couple of points. The bounds on the mass assigned to each couple of points reveal that, under suitable conditions, the support of any solution to the UOT is contained within a compact set that does not depend on the measures $\mu$ and $
u$, but only on the penalty function $\Dphi$ and the cost function $c$. We then introduce a truncated version of the UOT problem that fully leverages the sparsity of the optimal solution by introducing a parameter $R$ that saturates $c$. We show that any solution to the truncated problem naturally yields an approximation of the optimal solution for the standard UOT problem and bound the primal sub-optimality gap between the real solution and the solution induced by the truncated problem via a decreasing power-like function of $R$. Lastly, we study the convergence speed of the Pairwise Frank-Wolfe algorithm when applied to the truncated UOT problem and show that such routine is able to identify the support of the solution within a finite number of iterations.

title: Convergence of Adaptive Least Squares Finite Element Methods
abstract:
arXiv:2611.10278v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We consider a general class of operator equations $\mathcal B u=f$ where $\mathcal B:\mathbb U\to \mathbb L_2$ is a linear isomorphis from a Hilbert space $\mathbb U$ onto an ``$L_2$-type'' space $\mathbb L_2 = L_2(\Omega;\mathbb R^q)$. This covers weak first order formulations of stationary elliptic boundary value problems, the Stokes system or systems for linear elasticity as well as space-time formulations of heat or wave equations. Since an $L_2$-residual is uniformly equivalent to the corresponding error in the trial space norm reliable and efficient computable a posteriori error bounds are for free. In contrast to a matured theory of classical adaptive finite element methods, estblishing linear convergence - and eventually optimal complexity - in a least squares setting seems to have remained open. To a large extent this is due to the fact that least squares error indicators do not exhibit any explicit dependence on local mesh-sizes. In this paper we propose a rather different approach to establish under which circumstances standard D\"orfler-marking mesh refinement gives rise to linear convergence and rate optimality of adaptive least squares finite element methods as well. A central role is played by a new notion of {\em data-visibility} which is a structural property of the data rather than a smoothness condition.

title: Memoryless BFGS on a nonsmooth convex function: two new results
abstract:
arXiv:2611.10284v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We extend the analysis of Asl and Overton~\cite{AO2021} for memoryless BFGS (also known as L-BFGS-1) using an Armijo-Wolfe line search and applied to the nonsmooth convex function $f(x)=a|x^{(1)}|+\sum_{i=2}^n x^{(i)}$, where $n\ge2$ and $a \geq \sqrt{n-1}$. This function is unbounded below, so the method is successful if it generates function values diverging to $-\infty$, and fails otherwise. For scaled L-BFGS-1, we sharpen the sufficient condition for % az{convergence of the absolute normalized search directions} in Theorem~3.1 of failure in \cite{AO2021} from $a\ge2\sqrt{n-1}$ to $a\ge\sqrt{3(n-1)}$.
  For the unscaled version, we prove success for every $a$: either the method generates a direction along which no Armijo-Wolfe step exists, certifying unboundedness below, or its function values diverge to $-\infty$.
  Both results are consistent with the numerical experiments in \cite{AO2021}. Both proofs given here were derived with help from GPT 6 in discussions directed by the first author and corrected and rephrased afterward.

title: Costate-Conditioned Dynamic Programming for Parallel-in-Time Solution of Equality-Constrained Optimal Control Problems
abstract:
arXiv:2611.10286v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: When interior-point methods are applied to solve numerical trajectory optimisation problems, they spend most of their per-iteration time on a structured Newton--KKT system, associated to an equality-constrained linear-quadratic optimal control problem. Riccati-type algorithms exhibit linear complexity in the trajectory horizon. Parallel-in-time algorithms are able to reduce this to logaritmic complexity by distributing several subtrajectories over multiple cores and then stitch together the results by means of an associative scan. Existing exact formulations condition each subtrajectory on its terminal state. Each subproblem then carries the reachability to that terminal state explicitly as constraint rows. The associated reachability decision however is ill-conditioned for weakly actuated systems. In this work we condition each subtrajectory on the terminal costate instead. The resulting subproblems can now be computed by a free-end Riccati recursion without reachability carrying rows. This approach effectively compensates for the ill-conditioning of weakly actuated systems but requires additional bookkeeping with Lagrangian multipliers when stitching together the various subproblems. Numerically the method reproduces a direct solution of the primal-dual Newton-KKT system to $10^{-12}$ in relative terms, on a weakly controllable chain of masses, the accurracy rivals that of a sequential recursion, whereas terminal-state conditioning loses up to six digits or fails. Operation counts on a problem with 64 subtrajectories and a horizon of 4096 stages gives a speed-up of 26 compared with a sequential solve.

title: Calculation and Recurrence Relations of the Determinants of the Hessenberg - Toeplitz Matrices
abstract:
arXiv:2611.10291v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The determinant D(n) of a n x n Hessenberg - Toeplitz matrix is given as product of certain functions of its elements. A compact expression of D(n) is presented and recurrence relations involving determinants and matrix elements of the Hessenberg -Toeplitz matrices are found.

title: Sample complexity and scalability of adaptive-sampling trust-region methods for zeroth-order stochastic optimization --- Part I: common random numbers meet supermartingales
authors: Joseph Dzahini, Sara Shashaani, Coralia Cartis
abstract:
arXiv:2611.10296v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We analyze adaptive sampling stochastic model-based trust-region methods that build their models in random subspaces and use common random numbers (CRN) within an iteration, and obtain, within a STORM-type analysis, the first $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(\varepsilon^{-4})$ bound on the number of function evaluations needed to reach $\varepsilon$-stationarity, both almost surely and in expectation. The subspace model reduces the per-iteration computational cost, which allows scalability. The analysis relies on a general framework for the complexity of adaptive stochastic processes that carries the almost-sure analysis of ASTRO-DF into the STORM setting and adds expected bounds by a direct counting argument, without the renewal-reward argument of Blanchet et al. (2019). The bounds are obtained for two variants of a stochastic model-based trust-region method that differ in how the function evaluations used to measure progress are generated. The first algorithm, ASTRA-F, proceeds in a STORM-like manner: the trial point and the incumbent are re-evaluated on an independent set of replications, so that the estimates entering the acceptance test are independent of the model, as every existing STORM-type analysis requires their accuracy to be assessed conditionally on the model. The second, ASTRA-R, allows a practical approach: the trial point is evaluated on the replications already drawn to build the model, which avoids re-evaluating the incumbent, needs one adaptive sample size per iteration instead of two, and reduces the randomness entering the iteration. To our knowledge, no STORM-type analysis has been able to accommodate the latter approach as the accuracy of an estimate at a point chosen from the samples cannot be assessed conditionally on the model; we overcome this with a probabilistic chaining argument.

title: A metric characterization of free unitary quantum groups
abstract:
arXiv:2611.10299v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: For a compact matrix quantum group $G$ with a fundamental unitary representation $u$ of dimension at least two, the reduced operator norm of the self-adjoint main character satisfies $\left \|\chi_u+\chi_u^*\right \|_{C_r(G)}\geq2\sqrt2$. Within the category of free quantum groups of Kac type, it is known that the minimum $2\sqrt2$ is attained only by free unitary quantum groups. We establish this characterization in full generality, including the non-Kac setting: this minimum is attained if and only if $G$ is isomorphic to a free unitary quantum group $U_Q^+$ as compact matrix quantum groups.

title: Up or down by half: a family of Collatz-type maps
abstract:
arXiv:2611.10311v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Each Collatz step changes a positive integer by roughly half: odd inputs go up and even inputs go down. We vary the directions while keeping the step size. Write x=2^m k (k odd), and let S be a set of positive integers. Define T_S(x)=(3x+1)/2 if m=0, 3x/2 if m is in S, and k otherwise. The map T_S^- differs only at odd x, which it sends to (x+1)/2. The usual Collatz map is T_emptyset.
  Assuming the independence of 2-adic valuations along odd-to-odd steps yields random-walk models with drifts (1+rho(S))log_2(3)-2 for T_S and rho(S)log_2(3)-2 for T_S^-, where rho(S) is an explicit series. Every T_S^- is contracting; T_S is contracting exactly when rho(S)<2^34 (n<1.668*10^10 for S={1}) reaches one of at most five cycles; stopping-time statistics match the model to 3-5 digits.
  We study branching maps, where any member of a family may be applied at each step. Boundedness of a family implies boundedness of each member; in particular, boundedness of {T_emptyset,T_{3}} would imply that no Collatz orbit diverges. For {T_emptyset,T_{1}}, a rule depending only on x mod 32 has positive drift (10/17)log_2(9/8) for almost every 2-adic starting point. Thus almost all n have reachable sets containing values larger than n^1.05; residues modulo 2^L, L<=10, cannot prove unboundedness.
  Finally, we define unified maps in which valuations also determine the direction at odd inputs. The cases x=1 mod 4 govern their behavior: if they go down, every block is dominated by the corresponding Collatz map (and a census finds only the cycles (1), (2, 3) and (3, 5) with smallest element below 10^9); if they go up, the maps behave like T_S.

title: Characterizations of minimal Hermitian completions via moments and subdifferentials
abstract:
arXiv:2611.10323v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Given a Hermitian matrix $A_0$ and a real subspace $W$ of Hermitian matrices, we study the matrices $A_0+W_0$, $W_0\in W$, of minimal spectral norm, which we call $W$-minimal. The main motivation is the Hermitian matrix completion problem, where $W$ is spanned by the Hermitian matrix units corresponding to the unspecified entries. Our main tool is the moment of a subspace $S\subseteq\mathbb{C}^n$ relative to $W$, a compact convex subset of $\mathbb{R}^r$, $r=\dim(W)$, which we relate to the joint numerical range and to the $k$-dimensional field of a family of matrices. We compute the subdifferential of $\|A_0+W(x)\|$ in terms of the moments of the eigenspaces of the extreme eigenvalues of $A_0+W(x)$, and we obtain several equivalent characterizations of $W$-minimality: in terms of eigenvectors, of moments, of subdifferentials and of norm one functionals that annihilate $W$. When the identity belongs to $W$, every $W$-minimal matrix has balanced spectrum, and minimality is equivalent to the moments of the eigenspaces of the maximum and minimum eigenvalues having nonempty intersection; we show that this characterization fails if $I\notin W$. We illustrate the results with several examples, and we prove that the adjacency matrix of a connected graph is minimal for its completion problem if and only if the graph is complete bipartite.

title: Quenched large deviation estimates for skew product systems with the almost-sure fiber specification property
authors: Xue Liu, Xiaomin Zhou, Xiaoyao Zhou
abstract:
arXiv:2611.10350v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We establish quenched level-2 large deviation estimates for empirical measures of measurable skew products with compact metric fibers over an invertible ergodic measure-preserving transformation on a Polish space. Our hypotheses are formulated through lower and upper energy functions, which describe the exponential decay of conditional measures of fiber Bowen balls. Under almost-sure fiber specification, we prove lower bounds for open sets. Upper bounds for closed convex sets require only the upper energy condition, and upper semicontinuity of fiber entropy removes the convexity restriction. When these hypotheses hold with a common energy function \(T\), we obtain a quenched level-2 large deviation principle with a good rate function \(I_T(\rho)=\int T\,d\rho-h_\rho(F)\) on invariant measures with the prescribed base marginal, and \(+\infty\) otherwise. We also derive quenched level-1 large deviation principles for bounded continuous observables and a quenched Laplace principle. As an application, we consider skew products that are Anosov and topologically mixing on fibers. For Gibbs equilibrium states associated with random potentials $f$ having integrable two-sided Bowen variation, we construct bounded strictly positive common energy functions by coboundary corrections. This construction identifies the large deviation rate on invariant measures as \(\pi_F(f)-h_\rho(F)-\int f\,d\rho\), where \(\pi_F(f)\) denotes the fiber topological pressure.

title: Divide-and-Conquer is Tail- and Anomaly-Robust: Factor Model Estimation Without Moment Constraints
authors: Zetai Cen, Han Yan, Haeran Cho
abstract:
arXiv:2611.10358v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study robust estimation of elliptical factor models with abnormal observations and without requiring the existence of any positive moments. In particular, a divide-and-conquer (DC) estimator averages orthogonal projectors onto the full column spaces of small data blocks, and we rigorously establish its probability bound that allows weak and heterogeneous factors. The derived convergence rate is comparable to that of classical principal component estimators, up to the proportion of anomalies. Building on our DC estimator, we propose a split-sample tail- and anomaly-robust (STAR) estimator for the factor number using sample medians of successive projected coordinate ratios, which is shown consistent under mild conditions. Subsequent factor and common component estimation is also discussed, with the rates of convergence spelled out. Remarkably, given an upper bound on the true factor number, our suite of procedures are free from tuning, require no tail-dependent truncation threshold nor solving an optimization problem, admit parallel block computations, and hence has the same computational complexity as the classical principal component methods. Extensive experiments corroborate our theoretical findings, where DC and STAR are comparable and often outperform state-of-the-art competitors. We also illustrate our methods on a portfolio return dataset.

title: How good are spline spaces for the Kolmogorov $n$-width of a Sobolev ball?
abstract:
arXiv:2611.10371v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper studies the approximation power of polynomial splines on a uniform one-dimensional mesh. The quality of the best approximation of the unit ball of $H^{s}$ by an $n$-dimensional subspace, measured in the $L^{2}$ norm, is quantified by the sup-inf of that space: for each function in the Sobolev ball, take its minimal approximation error over the space, and then take the supremum of these errors over the ball. The infimum of this sup-inf over all $n$-dimensional spaces is the well-known Kolmogorov $n$-width $d_{n}$. Choosing the $n$-dimensional subspace to be the piecewise polynomial space of degree $k$ with smoothness $C^{\mu}$ ($-1\le\mu\le k-1$) gives our sup-inf $E$. The approximation accuracy of spline spaces is then examined by comparing $d_{n}$ and $E$. The two quantities are determined by two eigenvalue problems, through which we obtain a lower bound for $d_{n}$ and an upper bound for $E$. Under the restriction $k\ge s-1$, the upper bound for the error of the maximally smooth spline space ($\mu=k-1$) is asymptotically equal to the lower bound for $d_n$, showing that uniform $B$-splines are asymptotically optimal among all $n$-dimensional spaces. For $\mus-1$ and $\mu=k-2$ hold simultaneously. This reveals the superiority of $B$-splines in the sense of $n$-widths. Numerical experiments corroborate these bounds and, in some cases (e.g. the exception above), show that they are sharp.

title: Discrete-Time Zero-Sum Markov Games with Control, Stopping, and State-Dependent Discounting
abstract:
arXiv:2611.10396v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study a discrete-time two-player zero-sum stochastic game with control and stopping, where both players can stop the game, the discount factors depends on the states, and the running and terminal rewards may be unbounded. A contraction argument for the constrained Shapley equation establishes the existence of the value and a Nash equilibrium consisting of stationary controls and stopping times. We further provides algorithms for approximating the value and computing an $\varepsilon$-Nash equilibrium. A numerical example with state-dependent discount factors illustrates the results.

title: Basis selection, universal sampling discretization, and sampling recovery
authors: Feng Dai, Jiashu Ran, Vladimir N. Temlyakov
abstract:
arXiv:2611.10402v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: For every real $N$-dimensional subspace of $L_2$, we construct one orthonormal basis such that, for every $1\le v\le N$, at most $Cv\log(eN/v)$ positively weighted samples discretize the squared $L_2$ norm of all $v$-term combinations. Random rotations also give simultaneous weighted $L_p$ estimates and a sharp $C\log(eN)$ bound for the squared $L_2$ norm of the pointwise maximum. For prescribed coefficient classes, a change of measure yields sampling recovery estimates from $Cv\log^3(2v)$ samples under a lower Riesz inequality and a common square-integrable pointwise bound.

title: Directional Ergodic Theorems, Ergodicity, and Weak mixing for $\mathbb Z^2$-actions
authors: Chunlin Liu, Kairan Liu, Tao Yu
abstract:
arXiv:2611.10409v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this paper, we study Birkhoff and von Neumann type ergodic theorems for $\mathbb Z^2$-measure preserving systems along irrational directions. This leads us to a further investigation of directional ergodicity and weak mixing. Additionally, we show that our framework (dynamical definitions) is equivalent to the spectral definitions of directional ergodicity and weak mixing introduced by Robinson, Rosenblatt and \c{S}ahin \cite{RRS2023} for $\mathbb Z^2$-actions.
  We note that in their recent paper \cite{RS2026}, Robinson and \c{S}ahin established the equivalence between dynamical and spectral directional weak mixing for $\mathbb Z^2$-actions using an approach fundamentally different from the one employed in the present paper.

title: High-order long-time stable methods for the forced incompressible Navier--Stokes equations
authors: Fukeng Huang, Jie Shen, Xiaoming Wang
abstract:
arXiv:2611.10436v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present in this paper two scalar auxiliary variable (SAV) correction steps for constructing long-time stable schemes for the forced incompressible Navier--Stokes equations with no-slip boundary conditions. A main feature is that the same correction steps apply to any linear predictor satisfying the order and spatial regularity requirements in Assumption~P. Their construction and stability analysis are independent of the particular form of the predictor and require no energy estimate for it. The first correction uses a damped, shifted kinetic-energy variable to obtain a uniform-in-time $L^2$ bound in two and three dimensions, together with a weighted dissipation estimate. In two dimensions, the second correction combines a higher-energy auxiliary variable with a scalar relaxation to yield a uniform-in-time $H^1$ bound. Under the stated assumptions, these estimates hold on arbitrary positive time grids, without restrictions on step sizes or adjacent step ratios. We also derive eventual absorbing bounds; for the two-SAV scheme, these apply to the admissible initial class associated with fixed parameters. The generalized BDF schemes require one constant-coefficient Helmholtz solve per velocity component and one pressure Poisson solve per step; the second correction adds no field solve. Numerical experiments exhibit second-, third-, and fourth-order convergence for the tested BDF schemes and illustrate the long-time stability and efficiency of adaptive time stepping.

title: An introduction to discrete dynamics in condensed sets: orbits, periodic loci, and arithmetic examples
abstract:
arXiv:2611.10438v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We formulate discrete dynamics internally in the topos Cond of condensed sets. For an endomorphism $f\colon X\to X$, we construct orbit quotients, backward histories, preimage trees, and periodic loci as objects evaluated on profinite parameter spaces. The framework recovers global-section dynamics, fully faithfully embeds compact Hausdorff systems, characterizes the invertible extension, and is compatible with inverse limits. It organizes $p$-adic congruence towers and shows, for a Cantor-type non-Archimedean Julia set, that classical periodic points can be dense although the internal periodic locus is not isomorphic to the compact condensed Julia set.

title: Zeroth-Order Langevin Dynamics for Stochastic Nonconvex Optimization: Curvature Regularization and Non-Asymptotic Guarantees
abstract:
arXiv:2611.10461v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Zeroth-order methods provide a way to optimize stochastic nonconvex objectives using only noisy function evaluations. However, the smoothing inherent in their gradient estimators effectively modifies the objective being optimized. In particular, Gaussian smoothing with smoothing parameter $\eta>0$ induces, to leading order, an implicit Hessian-trace regularization, which motivates the study of the curvature-regularized objective of the form $f(x)+(\eta^2/2) tr(\nabla^2 f(x))$. We develop a non-asymptotic theory in the nonconvex setting for a class of algorithms called stochastic zeroth-order Langevin dynamics (ZOLD), which use only noisy function evaluations and do not have access to first- or higher-order derivative information, and derive excess-risk guarantees for the curvature-regularized objective. We first control the finite-time distribution of the ZOLD iterates in Wasserstein distance with respect to the Gibbs measure associated with the Gaussian-smoothed objective. An explicit coupling between the smoothing and inverse temperature parameters then quantifies the proximity of this measure to the Gibbs measure associated with the corresponding Hessian-trace-regularized objective. These distributional estimates in Wasserstein distance lead to excess-risk bounds for the curvature-regularized objective. Our analysis accommodates assumptions under which the stochastic function evaluations are allowed to have non-uniform dependence on the data stream. In addition, the constants in the non-asymptotic bounds do not rely on log-Sobolev or Poincar\'e inequalities as in prior zeroth-order Langevin analyses. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first non-asymptotic analysis of a zeroth-order Langevin method that simultaneously establishes excess-risk guarantees for a curvature-regularized objective and Wasserstein guarantees for the associated Gibbs measure in the nonconvex setting.

title: GEAR: A GPU-Accelerated Global Solver for Bounded Continuous Nonlinear Programs via Linear Bound Propagation
authors: Duo Zhou, Hesun Chen, Xiangru Zhong, Grani A. Hanasusanto, Huan Zhang
abstract:
arXiv:2611.10487v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present a novel GPU-accelerated global solver for constrained nonlinear programming (NLP) inspired by the efficient linear bound propagation framework in neural network (NN) verification. Existing work on NN verification, a problem that can be cast as feasibility detection for a nonlinear objective, demonstrated orders-of-magnitude speedups with the linear bound propagation-based framework when compared to traditional solvers. Extending this paradigm to global nonlinear programming requires addressing many challenges: a global constrained NLP solver must effectively exploit all, possibly unstructured, nonlinear constraints to improve the objective, whereas NN verification typically handles simple input box constraints over a well-structured NN and does not directly optimize an objective function. We address these challenges by fully exploiting the linear bounds produced by bound propagation: these linear bounds can be viewed as relaxations of nonlinear constraints and used to provide lower bounds, check infeasibility, and guide the search for a primal solution. In addition, we propose tighter linear relaxations for bilinear, quotient, and other commonly used nonlinear functions in NLP problems, and a projected augmented Lagrangian method tightly coupled to our dual solving procedure to produce primal solutions. Our method solves 421 of 505 bounded and continuous NLP problems in the GAMS and MINLPLib benchmarks under a 180-second limit, more than each of the six global solvers we compare with, including Gurobi and BARON (commercial), and SCIP (open-source). Sixteen of these problems are certified by none of the six global solvers; all of them contain exponential, logarithmic, or trigonometric terms, which are often challenging for traditional approaches. Project webpage is at https://verified-intelligence.github.io/GEAR.

title: A Trajectory-Aware Domain-Decomposed Multispace Reduced Basis Preconditioner for Parametric Helmholtz Problems
authors: An Ping, Zhichao Peng, Pengliang Yang
abstract:
arXiv:2611.10491v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Repeated solutions of parametric Helmholtz problems arise in multi-query applications such as sensitivity analysis and uncertainty quantification. Classical preconditioned iterative solvers do not automatically reuse low-dimensional structures across parameters. Multispace reduced basis (MSRB) preconditioners can exploit such structures by constructing iteration-specific reduced order models (ROMs) from training data, but storing global iteration-dependent bases incurs substantial memory costs. Building on trajectory-aware MSRB training, we develop a domain-decomposed MSRB (DD-MSRB) preconditioner for parametric Helmholtz systems truncated by perfectly matched layers (PMLs). Within flexible GMRES, each reduced space is trained on inverse-action snapshots along the Krylov trajectories generated by the ROM-based preconditioners applied in preceding iterations. To reduce storage, problem-adapted spatial partitions exploit heterogeneous local snapshot compressibility across the physical interior and the PML. Local basis dimensions in each subdomain are determined greedily under a global snapshot-error budget to balance approximation accuracy and storage. The resulting hybrid solver applies DD-MSRB preconditioning during the initial iterations to capture dominant cross-parameter modes and then switches, when necessary, to a shifted-Laplacian preconditioner to reduce error components poorly represented by the reduced spaces. Numerical experiments on two-dimensional half-space propagation, elliptic-obstacle scattering, and three-dimensional waveguides demonstrate significant acceleration over the shifted-Laplacian baseline and substantial memory savings relative to global MSRB. For the largest waveguide system, with 11.0 million unknowns, DD-MSRB reduces deployed ROM storage by 44.9% and mean online solve time by 30.2% compared with global MSRB.

title: Geometric Stochastic Dynamics and Fokker-Planck Equation on $\mathsf{T}\mathbb S^2$
abstract:
arXiv:2611.10493v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper develops a geometric (coordinate-free) stochastic model of a controlled point mass evolving on the unit two-sphere $\mathbb S^2$, together with the Fokker-Planck equation governing the probability density of the resulting stochastic process. The state manifold is the tangent bundle $\mathsf{T}\mathbb S^2$. The Levi-Civita connection of the round metric is used to construct the horizontal-vertical splitting of $\mathsf{T}(\mathsf{T}\mathbb S^2)$ and to convert the intrinsic second-order dynamics of the system into a first-order controlled vector field on $\mathsf{T}\mathbb S^2$. Endowing the tangent bundle with the Sasaki metric then permits stochastic perturbations to be introduced intrinsically and independently in horizontal, i.e., position, and vertical, i.e., velocity, directions. The corresponding infinitesimal generator is obtained in horizontal-vertical Hessian form. The probability density is defined with respect to the Sasaki Riemannian volume measure. The Fokker-Planck equation is derived intrinsically in both Stratonovich and It\^o forms. In the It\^o representation, a globally defined horizontal-vertical diffusion tensor yields a compact double-divergence Fokker-Planck PDE. No coordinates or embedded Euclidean representation of the sphere dynamics are used in the development. Numerical simulations illustrate the stochastic motion of a controlled particle ensemble on $\mathbb S^2$ toward an antipodal target configuration.

title: On naturality of cohomological support for small quantum groups
abstract:
arXiv:2611.10519v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We apply the theory of hypersurface support by Negron and Pevtsova to prove the naturality of cohomological support of the small quantum Borel groups, with respect to restriction to Levi subalgebras. This in turn implies naturality of cohomological support of the small quantum groups for modules that lift to Lusztig's big quantum group, for instance tilting modules. This allows us to make the recent conditional classification of tensor ideals of abelian type in the category of such tilting modules unconditional.

title: Error Estimates and Convergence Analysis for Learning Mechanism--AI Coupled Dynamical Systems
authors: Pengfei Song, Yanni Xiao, Yuan Lou, Shuangshuang Yin
abstract:
arXiv:2611.10520v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Mechanism--AI coupled dynamical systems retain known mechanisms while learning unknown dynamics from data. We study how neural approximation, numerical integration, finite observations, and optimization jointly affect the accuracy of this learning process. For time-dependent learned terms in a fixed compact admissible class, we derive a four-component objective error bound within an optimal control formulation. Explicit estimates are obtained for constrained ReLU approximation and Euler integration, with deterministic quadrature and random sampling treated separately. Under joint refinement, we establish $\Gamma$-convergence of the approximate objectives and show that approximate minimizers approach the continuous optimal set when the global optimization gaps vanish. We also derive conditional stability estimates for state-dependent learned terms. Numerical experiments with a susceptible--infected--recovered (SIR) model illustrate the analysis and show how solver resolution affects continuous-trajectory accuracy even when training losses are similar.

title: Removing the floor from Hoeffding and Bernstein inequalities for finite-population U-statistics
authors: Jianhang Ai, Yiming Chen, Ond\v{r}ej Ku\v{z}elka, Yuyi Wang
abstract:
arXiv:2611.10551v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Let $C$ be a uniformly sampled $n$-element subset of a finite population $D$ of size $N$, and let $U_C$ be the complete U-statistic of order $k$ built from a bounded kernel on the $k$-subsets of $D$. We prove a product inequality for the uniform distribution on $\binom{D}{n}$ and deduce from it the comparison $ \log \mathbb{E}\left[e^{\theta(U_C-\mathbb{E}U_C)}\right] \le \frac{n}{k}\log \mathbb{E}\left[e^{\frac{k\theta}{n}(Y-\mathbb{E}Y)}\right]$, where $Y$ is a single kernel value taken at a uniformly sampled $k$-subset of $D$. This yields Hoeffding, Bennett and Bernstein inequalities for $U_C$ with effective sample size $n/k$ in place of the $\lfloor n/k\rfloor$ available so far. The gain is negligible when $n$ is much larger than $k$, but it approaches a factor of two in the exponent when $k$ is close to $n$.

title: On Relative Greedy Weights
abstract:
arXiv:2611.10567v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Relative greedy weights were introduced by Li and Liu in [19] as a measure of information leakage in coordinated two-party wire-tap channels of type II when the adversary follows a greedy strategy. Their definition can be viewed as a relative version of the CEZ greedy weights, which are only locally greedy. In this paper, we revisit the concept of greediness and relative greediness introducing new measures, and we discuss other perhaps more relevant applications of relative greedy weights than the coordinated two-party wire-tap channel of type II. We pay special attention to bottom-up greedy weights, which correspond to an adversary with an ultimate greedy approach, and we present families of nested codes for which such weights are larger than the relative CEZ greedy weights.

title: Learning-Assisted Beamforming Optimization for Hybrid XL-RIS-Aided Communication
abstract:
arXiv:2611.10569v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Hybrid active-passive extremely large-scale reconfigurable intelligent surface (XL-RIS) architectures mitigate the double-hop path loss of passive RIS while enabling near-field spatial energy focusing, but impose a computationally intensive mixed discrete-continuous beamforming design problem under strict radio-frequency (RF) power constraints. This paper investigates a hybrid XL-RIS-assisted downlink multi-user multiple-input single-output (MU-MISO) system in the near-field regime. The joint optimization of the base station (BS) precoder, discrete XL-RIS phase shifts, and active-element amplification gains is addressed via a discrete coordinate ascent (DCA)-based alternating optimization (AO) framework, in which discrete variables are updated through local index-domain searches and the BS precoder is derived in closed form via a noise-aware minimum mean-square error (MMSE) criterion. To reduce the per-sample computational cost for XL-RIS apertures, a deep unfolding (DU) framework is proposed as a low-complexity alternative, unrolling a fixed number of Riemannian gradient ascent steps on the sum-rate objective and recovering the discrete phase configuration via quantized phasor projection, with one learnable step size per layer trained in a self-supervised manner. Numerical results under near-field spherical-wave channel models confirm that the DU framework achieves sum-rate performance close to the AO scheme with substantially lower and nearly constant runtime, and that both schemes consistently outperform manifold optimization under discrete hardware constraints.

title: Integrals of motion for the deformed $W$-algebra $W_{q,t}(D_l)$
abstract:
arXiv:2611.10580v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The deformed $W$-algebra $W_{q,t}(D_l)$ of type $D_l$ possesses an infinite family of commuting elements that can be viewed as a two-parameter deformation of the classical Hamiltonians for the KdV hierarchy of type $D_l$; these conserved charges are termed local integrals of motion (IMs). Concurrently, the quantum toroidal algebra $U_q(D_l^{"})$ of type $D_l$ admits four distinct representations via free field realizations, each corresponding to one of the four end nodes of the affine Dynkin diagram. Utilizing these representations, we associate an infinite set of commuting operators with each node, which we define as non-local integrals of motion. Both local and non-local integrals of motion act simultaneously on a shared Fock space consisting of $l+1$ free fields. We provide a direct, computational proof demonstrating that these local and non-local integrals of motion mutually commute.

title: Analytic criteria for criticality of subordinated Schr\"{o}dinger operators
abstract:
arXiv:2611.10614v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: For a subordinated Schr\"{o}dinger operator, we introduce a quantity that plays a role analogous to the bottom of the spectrum of a Schr\"{o}dinger operator, and establish analytic criteria for subcriticality, criticality and supercriticality of a subordinated Schr\"{o}dinger operator.

title: Sharp Constants and First-Order Asymptotics in a Bourgain--Brezis--Mironescu Formula for Riesz Potentials
abstract:
arXiv:2611.10656v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We investigate sharp constants and asymptotic properties of a pointwise inequality of Bourgain--Brezis--Mironescu type in dimension \(n\geq2\), involving Riesz potentials and Spector's nonlinear fractional differential operator \(\mathcal D^\alpha\) of order \(0<\alpha<1\). For every \(n\geq3\) and \(0<\alpha<1\), we determine the optimal constant without symmetry restrictions and prove that it is attained by smooth radially monotone functions centered at the evaluation point. The proof combines geodesic-flow invariance, kernel monotonicity, and circular rearrangement. In dimension two, we establish the leading-order asymptotic behavior of the optimal constant and derive an explicit formula in the radial class. We further refine the pointwise limit established by A. Claros and C. P\'erez [Bourgain--Brezis--Mironescu formula for Riesz potentials, Adv. Math. 503 (2026), Art. 111226] by obtaining an explicit first-order correction with a quadratic remainder uniform in the spatial variable. Finally, we strengthen their convergence-in-measure result on compact subsets for functions in \(W^{1,1}(\mathbb R^n)\) by establishing almost-everywhere convergence as \(\alpha\to1^-\), without passing to a subsequence.

title: Port-Hamiltonian Systems Beyond Joules: A Review of Unexpected Application Domains
abstract:
arXiv:2611.10695v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The port-Hamiltonian framework was built for mechanical and electrical systems, where the Hamiltonian is stored energy and the ports carry power. Over the past fifteen years it has spread to chemistry, cell biology, fusion plasmas, musical instruments, district heating, electricity markets, macroeconomics, predator-prey ecology, optimization algorithms and neural-network training. This review maps that spread. We classify each application by what its Hamiltonian really is: physical energy, a thermodynamic potential such as free energy or exergy, or an abstract storage function with no energetic meaning. The review keeps only sources whose bibliographic record we checked against Crossref. The picture that emerges is a continuum. Where a genuine thermodynamic potential exists, the theory is deep and constructive. Where the energy is borrowed, the framework still pays off through compositional interconnection and dissipation inequalities, but the work is younger and scattered. We close with a set of deliberately speculative research directions, including open port-Hamiltonian models of epidemics, opinion dynamics and supply chains, and learned port-Hamiltonian digital twins for structural health monitoring.

title: A Prey-Predator Framework for Tumor-Immune Dynamics: Circuit-Based Modeling with Hilfer-Katugampola Fractional Derivatives
abstract:
arXiv:2611.10727v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This study focuses on modeling tumor--immune interactions through a fractional-order prey--predator framework, where tumor cells act as prey and immune effector cells as predators. To capture the hereditary and memory effects inherent in biological systems, we employ the Hilfer--Katugampola fractional derivative, which flexibly interpolates between Riemann--Liouville and Caputo formulations. In addition, a circuit-based analogy is introduced to map tumor proliferation, immune regulation, and therapeutic interventions onto resistive, capacitive, and inductive elements, providing intuitive interpretation of the dynamics. Analytical investigations, including equilibrium analysis and stability criteria, are conducted across varying fractional orders. Numerical simulations reveal that lower fractional orders lead to delayed oscillations, prolonged tumor persistence, and increased sensitivity to treatment strategies compared with classical integer-order models. The integration of fractional calculus with circuit analogies offers novel insights into tumor--immune dynamics and supports the design of memory-aware therapeutic interventions.

title: Performance Analysis of Entanglement Swapping DV-QKD over MIMO FSO Channels
authors: Sushil Kumar, Soumya P. Dash, George C. Alexandropoulos
abstract:
arXiv:2611.10743v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper studies multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) free-space optical (FSO) quantum communication systems employing polarization-encoded discrete-variable quantum key distribution (DV-QKD), based on entanglement swapping, with the goal of extending secure communications beyond the reach of a direct link. The FSO channels are subject to atmospheric absorption, diffraction, beam wander, pointing errors, and turbulence-induced fading, while background noise and detector imperfections degrade the performance. An eavesdropper controlling the channels and the relay is also considered. To analyze the performance of the considered system, both hops MIMO channels are decomposed into parallel spatial eigenchannels via singular value decomposition (SVD), photon loss is modeled using Kraus operators, and a threshold-detector model is developed for the relay. Based on these models, closed-form per-eigenchannel expressions for the relay gain are derived, which are then used to obtain expressions for the quantum bit error rate (QBER) and the secret key rate (SKR). Numerical results demonstrate that entanglement swapping maintains a low QBER over longer distances than direct transmission, extending the communication range beyond the noise-limited cutoff of the direct link, at the cost of a lower SKR at short distances. The crossover distance beyond which entanglement swapping prevails is determined mainly by the background noise and the detector technology, and it is demonstrated to increase with MIMO configurations. Moreover, the reach gain is shown to be maximized for a midpoint relay. Finally, since each swapping event requires a single-pair emission from both sources, a near-deterministic entangled-photon source is required, which spontaneous parametric down-conversion sources do not provide at practical key rates, whereas MIMO substantially relaxes this requirement.
